text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Tuesda.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Malawi Housing Corporation (MHC) chairperson Joyce Banda said the parastatal faces possible closure or that some staff may be retrenched following a High Court injunction granted on Friday stopping it from collecting new rents effected in Aril, last year.

- Police arrested Civil Servants Trade Union (CSTU) vice president Mike Gondwe in Mzuzu, northern Malawi as he addressed a small group of striking workers. Malawi civil servants went on strike to push for a 100 percent wage increase.

- Former President Kamuzu Banda's defence lawyer, London-based Bernard O'Sullivan, requested the High Court to drop fraud charges against him (Banda) on grounds of ill health. Government charged Banda and others of illegally funding a grammar school, Kamuzu Academy, in his home district with more than $9 million between 1985 and 1994.

- The Norwegian Confederation of Trade Unions has threatened to team up with other unions in the international trade union movement to support Malawi's striking civil servants who began a nationwide strike on April 7 to push for a 100 percent wage inrease.
